verses.text: All the kings west of the Jordan heard what happened—including the hill-country kings, lowland kings, and everyone along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon. That meant Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. 👑
They linked up and made one plan: fight Joshua and Israel. ⚔️
But when Gibeon’s people heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, 🏙️
they went with a trick. They dressed up like travelers from far away, loaded old sacks onto their donkeys, and brought wineskins that were worn out and patched up. 🫏
They wore beat-up sandals and old clothes, and all their travel bread was dry and moldy. 🥖
They came to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and told him and Israel’s men, ‘We’re from a far-off country. So now, make a treaty with us.’ 🤝
Israel’s men said to the Hivites, ‘What if you actually live around here? How could we make a treaty with you?’ 🧐
They told Joshua, ‘We’re your servants.’ Joshua asked, ‘Who are you, and where did you come from?’ 🗣️
They answered, ‘Your servants came from a really far country because of the name of Yahweh your God. We’ve heard all about his reputation—everything he did in Egypt, 📣
‘and everything he did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived at Ashtaroth. 👑
‘Our elders and everyone back home told us, “Pack supplies for the trip, go meet them, and tell them, ‘We’re your servants. Make a treaty with us.’”’ 🎒
‘This bread was still hot when we packed it at home the day we left to come see you. But look now—it’s dry and moldy. 🥖
‘These wineskins were brand new when we filled them, but now they’re torn up. Our clothes and sandals are worn out from the long trip.’ 👞
The Israelite leaders sampled their food, but they didn’t ask Yahweh what he thought. 🍞
Joshua made peace with them and promised they could live. The assembly’s leaders swore an oath to them. 🤝
Three days after making the treaty, Israel heard the truth: these people were neighbors who lived nearby. 🕰️
On the third day, Israel packed up and reached their towns: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim. 🗺️
Israel didn’t attack them because the assembly’s leaders had sworn an oath to them by Yahweh, Israel’s God. So the whole assembly grumbled at the leaders. 😠
But all the leaders answered the crowd, ‘We swore to them by Yahweh, Israel’s God. So we can’t touch them now. ✋
‘Here’s what we’ll do: let them live, or we’ll bring Yahweh’s anger on ourselves over the oath we swore.’ ⚖️
The leaders told them, ‘Let them live.’ So the Gibeonites became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole assembly, just as the leaders had said. 🪵
Joshua called them in and asked, ‘Why did you trick us by saying, “We live really far away,” when you’re right here among us? 🧐
‘So now you’re under a curse. Some of you will always be slaves—woodcutters and water carriers for my God’s house.’ ⚠️

They answered Joshua, ‘Your servants were clearly told Yahweh your God commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and wipe out everyone living there. We were terrified for our lives because of you, so we did this. 😟
‘And now, look—we’re in your hands. Do whatever seems good and right to you.’ 🙏
So Joshua did just that: he rescued them from the Israelites’ hands, and they weren’t killed. 🛡️
That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the assembly and for Yahweh’s altar, at the place Yahweh would choose. They still do that to this day. 🪵
